name: Cleaning and janitorial companies

problems.words: Cleaners don't turn up and we find out when the customer calls angry
quick_ideas: Ask every cleaner to send a short "reached" message on arrival, so a no-show is known before the customer calls
Keep one or two standby cleaners each day, so a gap can be filled fast.

workzap_build.text: Check-in and check-out with location and before/after photos, with an alert to the office the moment a cleaner hasn't checked in on time, for every job every day.

problems.ask_first: How many cleaners are working for you right now?
problems.free_stops: Check-in method, alert timing and standby rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which jobs this week were confirmed by staff but still started late or empty, so the weak points in attendance become clearer.
Give one person the evening job of checking tomorrow's roster against staff replies, so surprises are caught before customers complain.

problems.words: Bookings come by WhatsApp, calls and the app and we double-book cleaners
quick_ideas: Put every booking, from any channel, into one shared calendar, so clashes show at once
Make one person responsible for assigning cleaners.

workzap_build.text: You would see every booking from chat, calls and the web land in one calendar, with cleaners assigned by area and availability and double bookings blocked.

problems.free_stops: Assignment rules and booking flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count bookings received from each channel that needed moving after assignment this week, so the busiest source of clashes stands out.
Keep one notebook page as the only booking list for all incoming jobs, so cleaner assignments stop colliding across channels.

problems.words: Quality depends completely on which cleaner goes
quick_ideas: Write one short checklist per service type, so every cleaner covers the same ground
Ask for before/after photos of bathrooms and kitchens, so quality can be checked.

workzap_build.text: A job checklist per service type with photo proof and a rating request to the customer after every job, so quality is measured per cleaner.

problems.ask_first: What do customers complain about most?
problems.free_stops: Checklist content and rating flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare complaint notes by service type and by cleaner this week, so you see where standards vary the most.
Give one supervisor the job of doing the same end of job spot check each day, so every branch is judged the same way.

problems.words: Cash collected by cleaners from homes doesn't reach the office in full
quick_ideas: Send customers the amount due by message before the job, so both sides know the figure
Match each cleaner's cash to their completed jobs at day's end.

workzap_build.text: A cash log per cleaner per day, matched against completed home jobs.

problems.free_stops: Matching rules and variance flags are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many home jobs ended with cash due but no same day office handover, so weak collection points stand out.
Keep one notebook at the office for every returned cash envelope, so handovers stop getting disputed between cleaners and staff.

problems.words: Chemicals and consumables run out fast
quick_ideas: Record what each team or site is issued this week, so usage can be compared
Compare issues against jobs done once, to spot the outliers.

workzap_build.text: A consumables issue log per team or site, with usage against jobs done and low-stock alerts.

problems.ask_first: How are chemicals and supplies given out?
problems.free_stops: Usage benchmarks and alert rules are in the solution document; chemical handling follows product safety instructions.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many packs or bottles leave storage for each team this week, so unusually heavy usage stands out by crew.
Give one store key holder the job of noting every item issued in one notebook, so stock stops disappearing between handovers.

problems.words: Contract sites have fewer cleaners than we bill for
quick_ideas: Check headcount at each contract site against the invoice once this week
Share a daily attendance sheet with the client, so they see it before they check.

workzap_build.text: A site headcount register with a daily attendance report sent to the client every day.

problems.ask_first: How does the client check the headcount?
problems.free_stops: Report format and attendance rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk each contract site once this week and count cleaners actually present during billed hours, so short staffing is measured clearly.
Give one supervisor the job of confirming site attendance at the same time each day, so billing matches what the client receives.

problems.words: Customers book once and never again
quick_ideas: Ask each customer after a job whether they'd like a regular slot
Contact recent one-off customers who agreed to hear from you.

workzap_build.text: Repeat-booking reminders and regular-plan options for customers who opted in.

problems.ask_first: Do you contact customers again after a job?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and plan structure are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many one time cleaning customers booked again within the same week, so the repeat gap is measured in your own routine.
Give one person a fixed time each afternoon to note which finished jobs should be offered another slot, so follow up stops slipping away.

problems.words: Corporate clients pay after sixty to ninety days
quick_ideas: Invoice on the same date every month, so the clock starts on time
List unpaid invoices by age and follow up the oldest.

workzap_build.text: Corporate invoicing and receivables tracking with reminders on schedule.

problems.ask_first: How long do corporate clients take to pay?
problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule and escalation are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this month's bill sending dates with each corporate client's usual approval window, so avoidable waiting days become visible.
Give one office person a fixed weekly slot to review overdue corporate bills, so follow up stays regular across long payment cycles.

problems.words: Transport between jobs wastes hours and fuel
quick_ideas: Group tomorrow's jobs by area before assigning, so cleaners stay in one zone
Note travel time for a week, to see the worst routes.

workzap_build.text: Scheduling that groups jobs by area and orders each team's day.

problems.ask_first: How do cleaners get to jobs?
problems.free_stops: Routing rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many crews crossed the same busy area more than once in a day, so wasted driving patterns are easier to spot.
Make one dispatcher own tomorrow's area grouping in one notebook each evening, so crews leave with tighter local runs.

problems.words: Turnover is so high we're always hiring and training
quick_ideas: Ask leavers why they left, so patterns show
Pair each new cleaner with an experienced one for the first jobs.

workzap_build.text: An onboarding and training checklist for every new hire.

problems.free_stops: The onboarding plan is in the solution document; labour-law questions go to a professional.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many new cleaners leave before finishing their early weeks this month, so the worst stage of dropout shows.
Give one supervisor the job of welcoming every new cleaner at the end of each shift, so early frustration gets noticed sooner.

never_say: Any guidance on mixing chemicals, bleach or acids, mould hazards, or facade and rope-access work.
Any help investigating or naming a cleaner accused of theft.
Any help hiring without valid permits, withholding passports, underpaying or faking headcount on invoices.
Any recording of cleaners' or customers' names, addresses, door codes, keys or ID/visa details.
Anything other than emergency services or the poison centre first for chemical exposure, falls, injury or fire.

sample_reply.person: Cleaners late jaati hain ya jaati hi nahi, aur pata customer ke gusse wale call se chalta hai. Koi hal batayen.
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har cleaner job pe pohanchte hi office ko ek chhota sa message bheje, taake na pohanchne ka pata customer se pehle chale.
Doosra, roz ek do standby cleaners rakhein, taake khali jagah jaldi bhari ja sake.
Pakke hal ke liye Workzap ye banwa sakta hai: har job ka check-in, aur waqt pe check-in na ho to office ko foran alert.
